question: Consider the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x)=4x+3$. Find $f^{-1}$ and verify the inverse using composition.
explanation:
Determination of the inverse
Let
$$y=f(x)=4x+3.$$
Solving for $x$, we obtain
$$x=\frac{y-3}{4}.$$
Hence,
$$f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x-3}{4}.$$

Verification of $f^{-1}\circ f$
$$f^{-1}(f(x))=\frac{(4x+3)-3}{4}=x.$$

Verification of $f\circ f^{-1}$
$$f\left(f^{-1}(x)\right)=4\left(\frac{x-3}{4}\right)+3=x.$$

Conclusion
Both compositions are the identity function. Thus, $f$ is invertible and
$$f^{-1}(x)=\frac{x-3}{4}.$$
